name: Hard-coded Indian payment-gateway merchant secret
attack_scenario: Anyone with repo access, a decompiled APK, or a leaked container layer reads the merchant salt and can forge valid payment-success signatures/checksums — completing orders without paying, tampering with amounts, or replaying webhooks — because the entire trust model of these gateways rests on that one secret staying private.
negative_test_hint: place a live-looking secret such as "rzp_live_Ab1Cd2Ef3Gh4Ij5K" directly in source and assert the review rejects it, requiring an environment or secret-manager lookup

exemplar.explanation: Indian PSP integration guides (Razorpay, PayU, CCAvenue, PhonePe, Paytm, Cashfree) all hinge on a server-side merchant secret/salt/working-key used to sign and verify payment requests; CERT-In fintech advisories and numerous public GitHub leaks show these baked into source constantly in outsourced Java/PHP/Node code. Loading the secret from an environment variable or secret manager keeps it out of the codebase and out of leaked artifacts.
